title: Grids and matrices
summary: A list of rows: read cells with grid[row][col], visit every cell with two loops, and avoid shared rows.

sections.heading: A list of rows
body: A grid is a list where each item is a row, and each row is a list of cells. `grid[row][col]`: the row comes first.

sections.heading: Visiting every cell
body: Two loops, one inside the other, visit every cell. Swapping which loop is outside lets you read the grid column by column. This turns rows into columns (a "transpose").

python.code:
grid = [
    [1, 2, 3],
    [4, 5, 6],
]
columns = [[row[c] for row in grid] for c in range(len(grid[0]))]
print(columns)

sections.heading: Every row must be its own list
body: Filling a grid with the same row object makes every row the same list, so changing one cell changes the whole column. Create a fresh row for each position.

python.code:
shared = [[0, 0]] * 2
shared[0][0] = 9
print(shared)

separate = [[0, 0] for _ in range(2)]
separate[0][0] = 9
print(separate)

mistakes: Assuming the grid is square: use the row count and the column count separately.
